hook.line: At the EPS counter and on every official form, the rules arrive in the same stiff phrase. Learn to read it, and you stop guessing what the clerk wants from you.
hook.en: It's compulsory to show the prescription.

examples.en: It's compulsory to show the prescription.
It's compulsory to bring your ID.

examples.es: Es obligatorio pagar antes de entrar.
examples.en: It's compulsory to pay before going in.

examples.es: No es obligatorio, pero se recomienda.
examples.en: It isn't compulsory, but it's recommended.

examples.es: Es obligatorio que todos los pacientes lleguen temprano.
examples.en: It's compulsory for all patients to arrive early.

rule:
*Es obligatorio* + infinitive says something is required by a rule: *Es obligatorio llevar casco*. Nothing goes between them, no *de*, no *que*.

*No es obligatorio* only means you don't have to. It does not mean forbidden: for a ban, use *está prohibido*.

When you say who has to do it, *que* appears and the verb changes: *Es obligatorio que todos lleguen temprano*. Just recognise that form for now.

It sounds official. With a person, you will use *tienes que*.
smallPrint: Teachers call the verb after *que* the subjunctive, and *es obligatorio* an impersonal expression of obligation.

options: Wearing a helmet is not compulsory.

yourTurn.prompt: Choose the right form and type the whole sentence (Wearing a helmet is compulsory): ___ llevar casco. (*Es obligatorio* / *No es obligatorio*)
yourTurn.why: It is required, so there is no *no*.

yourTurn.prompt: Choose the right form and type the whole sentence (You don't have to wear a helmet): ___ llevar casco. (*Es obligatorio* / *No es obligatorio*)
yourTurn.why: You don't have to is *no es obligatorio*.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: It's compulsory to show the prescription.
yourTurn.why: *Es obligatorio* goes straight into the infinitive.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: It's compulsory to bring your ID.
yourTurn.why: The infinitive *traer* follows with no extra word.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: It's compulsory to pay before going in.
yourTurn.answer: Es obligatorio pagar antes de entrar.
yourTurn.why: *Antes de* plus an infinitive says "before going in".

yourTurn.prompt: Make it negative: Es obligatorio pagar antes de entrar.
yourTurn.answer: No es obligatorio pagar antes de entrar.
yourTurn.why: *No* in front turns the rule off.

yourTurn.prompt: Say it isn't compulsory but it's recommended.
yourTurn.answer: No es obligatorio, pero se recomienda.
yourTurn.why: *Pero se recomienda* adds the soft advice.

pitfalls.why: Almost. The infinitive follows directly, with no *de*.

pitfalls.wrong: No es obligatorio entrar sin cita.
pitfalls.right: No está permitido entrar sin cita.
pitfalls.why: *No es obligatorio* only means you don't have to; for a ban, use *está prohibido*.
After *es obligatorio* the verb stays in its infinitive form.

personal: Think of a rule where you live or work. Write one thing that is compulsory and one that is not, with *es obligatorio* and *no es obligatorio*.
